title: OCR y Document AI
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S24.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts adjudicated USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S21-S23 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED. S24 cannot treat an S23 download path, short digest, trace label or resumed run as trustworthy provenance without a persisted independently validated artifact.
usable: digital PDF and scanned-image PDF are different acquisition modes
a mismatch is not a fraud conclusion
full evidence should remain separable from automated decisions
not_creditable: S23 download.path persisted the source document after browser close
S23 short SHA prefix is authoritative artifact identity
S23 retry/checkpoint guarantees one unique current document
S22 approval is bound to exact downstream content
S21 reporting payload and provenance are fully reconciled

roadmap_expectation.T1: Imagen: DPI, deskew, crop y contraste; ruido y orientación
roadmap_expectation.T2: OCR: idiomas, layout y confidence; texto, tablas y pares clave–valor
roadmap_expectation.T3: Extracción: schema y normalización; validación cross-field y cola de revisión
roadmap_expectation.T4: Evaluación: golden set sintético, exactitud por campo y cobertura; privacidad, archivos hostiles y fallback
roadmap_expectation.gate: extrae campos de documentos sintéticos, conserva bounding boxes/evidencia, abstiene bajo confidence y mide cada campo crítico

live_site.evidence: Public page exposes Section 24 'OCR Document AI' with the canonical gate text. Hydrated theory body is not exposed by the public text surface, so render-only defects were not invented.

checks: preprocess_meta reports dpi=200 while source_dpi remains 96 and no raster pixels were changed
fix_orientation returns an automatic-looking orientation even when best score is 0.4 and silently selects the first key on a tie
a raw Tesseract confidence of 55 passes the lesson's 0.85 threshold unless explicitly normalized to 0.55
kv_from_lines silently overwrites the first RUC when the same key appears twice
norm_total('1,150.00') returns 1.15 although the prose says that EN-thousands format must be rejected/out-of-policy
norm_total('1e3') returns 1000.0 despite scientific notation not being part of the documented money grammar
norm_ruc('20Ñ123456789') and norm_ruc('20💥123456789') silently strip the unexpected character and return 20123456789
validate() raises KeyError when total is missing instead of accumulating a review reason
field_acc([{ruc_pred:None,ruc_true:None}], 'ruc') returns 1.0 and field_acc([], field) raises ZeroDivisionError
coverage_auto=7/(7+3)=0.7 becomes 0.35 when five rejects and five OCR failures from the same intake are included
gate_file raises KeyError when mime or n_bytes metadata is missing
a spoofed payload declared application/pdf passes the implemented layer-1 gate because bytes/signature are never inspected

external_research.finding: Tesseract documents image preprocessing, deskew/noise/borders and says it generally works best around at least 300 dpi; changing metadata alone is not image resampling or restoration.
ResultIterator::Confidence is documented as percent probability on 0.0-100.0, so any 0-1 course contract needs an explicit normalization boundary.

Document entities/layouts carry confidence plus page/bounding references; evaluation exposes precision/recall/F1 at specific confidence levels, supporting threshold evaluation rather than an isolated magic cutoff.
Digitally-born PDFs should generally use native text extraction rather than rasterizing everything to OCR; scanned and OCRed PDFs are distinct modes.
Content-Type is spoofable; secure file admission is defense-in-depth including signatures/content validation, safe storage, resource limits and sandboxing.
Decimal is designed for exact decimal/accounting arithmetic; binary float is inappropriate where strict monetary equality/rounding invariants matter.

findings.evidence: Reference says the input is 'Una descarga verificada del adaptador web de S23'.
findings.attack: S23's real sketch returns a temporary download path after context close and its verification/hash contract remains unearned.
findings.defense: Curricular continuity needs a source artifact from S23.
findings.impact: OCR can begin from a stale, missing, duplicated or wrong source document.
findings.repair: Require a persisted source file with full SHA-256, size/type/content validation, browser_run_id and uniqueness/currentness evidence before S24 intake.

findings.evidence: Theory begins from a scanned-image model and provides no native-text bypass for digitally-born PDFs.
findings.attack: S21 already distinguishes digital PDFs from image/OCR cases; OCRing a native text PDF needlessly discards stronger information.
findings.defense: The opening explicitly talks about an 'factura escaneada' and S24 is the OCR-focused section.
findings.impact: Learner can generalize OCR as the default path for every PDF.
findings.repair: Add a routing gate: native digital text -> text extraction; raster/image or unusable text layer -> OCR; preserve the chosen mode in provenance.

findings.evidence: Canonical theory operates on metadata dicts and pre-supplied OCR tokens; no theory block sends a synthetic image/PDF through an OCR engine.
findings.attack: Roadmap gate says extract fields from synthetic documents, not merely parse observations invented before the function is called.
findings.defense: Fake adapters are appropriate for deterministic unit tests and are honestly labeled.
findings.impact: Learner can satisfy the apparent OCR gate without demonstrating OCR acquisition, page rendering or engine output at all.
findings.repair: Retain fake unit tests but add at least one tiny synthetic image/PDF fixture executed through a real/local OCR adapter or controlled deterministic OCR fixture that starts from pixels.

findings.evidence: preprocess_meta sets out['dpi']=max(source_dpi,200), so a 96-dpi source becomes dpi=200 without any raster operation.
findings.attack: The prose correctly says upscaling does not recover detail; changing the metadata field creates an even stronger false claim because no pixels changed at all.
findings.defense: Comments call this a planned metadata decision rather than OpenCV processing.
findings.impact: Downstream gates can treat a 96-PPI source as if it met the 200 threshold.
findings.repair: Keep source_ppi immutable; record target_ppi/resample_planned separately. Never use a synthetic 'dpi' overwrite as evidence that capture quality improved.

findings.evidence: Prose recommends capture at >=300 PPI effective, while code/callout make >=200 the passing lab floor.
findings.attack: The learner is given two different minima with no rationale for when 200 is sufficient.
findings.defense: Tesseract documentation says ~300 is generally beneficial, not a universal hard failure threshold; a 200 lab floor can be a deliberate simplification.
findings.impact: Quality gates become arbitrary rather than evidence-based.
findings.repair: State explicitly: 200 is a didactic warning floor only; 300 is the preferred capture target; calibrate by font size/corpus and actual OCR evaluation.

findings.evidence: deskew_applied=True, skew_deg=0.0, crop_box and contrast are emitted although no raster is deskewed/cropped/contrasted.
findings.attack: Names such as '*_applied' assert completed transformations, not plans.
findings.defense: Comments disclose the simulation.
findings.impact: Audit flags can say the image was transformed when nothing happened to it.
findings.repair: Rename to *_required/*_planned in metadata-only exercises; only write *_applied after a real transform and bind it to a processed-image hash.

findings.evidence: Every image gets a fixed 2% crop while the callout requires that crop not cut a seal/total.
findings.attack: No content-preservation check proves the 2% border is safe for a particular page.
findings.defense: The fixture is synthetic and the crop is explicitly didactic.
findings.impact: A real adaptation of the example can delete edge evidence while reporting a successful preprocess.
findings.repair: Make crop candidate-driven, verify content/bounds against the source, preserve pre/post previews or transform metadata, and fail to manual crop when uncertain.

findings.evidence: fix_orientation returns max score unconditionally; the <0.5 manual_orient rule appears only in prose/callout, and ties are not handled.
findings.attack: Runtime returns (0,0.4) for a low-confidence case and silently chooses the first orientation on an equal-score tie.
findings.defense: The function returns the score so a caller could decide.
findings.impact: The executable contract does not implement the quality gate it teaches.
findings.repair: Return status auto/manual; require minimum score plus ambiguity margin; ties/near-ties -> manual_orient.

findings.evidence: Learning outcome says correct noise before OCR; denoise_binary merely flips synthetic 1 flags to 0 and never modifies image data.
findings.attack: The student does not learn or demonstrate a denoise operation.
findings.defense: The function explicitly says it is a contract simulation.
findings.impact: Outcome wording exceeds demonstrated competence.
findings.repair: Either narrow the outcome to choosing/logging a denoise policy or add one real image-processing example and compare before/after OCR quality.

findings.evidence: T2-A sorts tokens by (y0,x0) while warning not to concatenate columns blindly.
findings.attack: Global y/x sorting is exactly the kind of heuristic that can interleave multi-column content.
findings.defense: Advanced multi-column layout is declared out of scope.
findings.impact: The limitation is stated but the simple algorithm is presented as 'orden de lectura'.
findings.repair: Name it single-column-only; add a two-column counterexample that must abstain or route to a layout-aware adapter.

findings.evidence: Course contract and threshold use confidence 0-1; opening callout allows TesseractAdapter when installed.
findings.attack: Tesseract ResultIterator::Confidence is documented on 0-100. A raw 55 would pass conf>=0.85 unless explicitly divided by 100.
findings.defense: A well-written adapter could normalize the engine value.
findings.impact: Without an explicit adapter boundary, low-confidence real OCR can be autoaccepted by two orders of magnitude.
findings.repair: Define adapter_confidence_01 = clamp(raw_conf/100) for Tesseract and test 55 -> 0.55; log engine/raw scale/normalized value.

findings.evidence: Token confidences are treated as field confidences with one universal 0.85 threshold.
findings.attack: Fields may span multiple tokens and confidence meaning differs by engine/entity level; threshold quality should be evaluated per field/corpus.
findings.defense: 0.85 is explicitly labeled a didactic lab threshold.
findings.impact: Learner may mistake a convenient cutoff for a calibrated probability of correctness.
findings.repair: Define token->field aggregation and evaluate threshold curves on the same golden set; keep 0.85 visibly didactic.

findings.evidence: The course promises bbox lets a reviewer highlight the value on the original, while preprocessing includes crop, deskew and rotation.
findings.attack: Those transforms change coordinates. bbox on the processed page cannot be overlaid on the original without transform lineage or the exact processed rendition.
findings.defense: T4-B later mentions page dimensions and a revisable rendition conceptually.
findings.impact: The central evidence rectangle can point to the wrong region.
findings.repair: Persist page index, coordinate space, processed dimensions, source/processed hashes and transform matrix; review against the exact rendition that produced the bbox or invert the transform.

findings.evidence: Canonical field output names source_doc_id/schema_version but code never binds fields to full source hash, processed page hash, engine/version, language/config or preprocessing version.
findings.attack: The job relevance promises auditable evidence and reproducibility.
findings.defense: The section is contract-first and some metadata is described in prose.
findings.impact: A reviewer cannot reproduce which bytes/config produced a field.
findings.repair: Emit source_sha256, page, processed_sha256, preprocess_config/version, OCR engine/model/version/lang, schema_version and field bbox/confidence with each run.

findings.evidence: kv_from_lines returns only {key:value}; it drops bbox/confidence and duplicate keys overwrite silently.
findings.attack: The adjacent paragraph/callout says evidence is value+bbox+conf; runtime duplicate RUC keeps only the last value.
findings.defense: The code is a minimal string parsing exercise.
findings.impact: Ambiguous OCR evidence can be silently collapsed into one authoritative-looking field.
findings.repair: Return a list/candidates per key with value, conf, bbox, page/source; duplicate competing values -> ambiguity reason/review.

findings.evidence: Schema declares total float; line sums and 0.01 reconciliation use binary floats.
findings.attack: S02 established Decimal/integer-cent semantics for PEN, and Python Decimal docs specifically recommend exact decimal arithmetic for accounting invariants.
findings.defense: The lab values shown happen to be exactly simple enough to print cleanly.
findings.impact: S24 regresses the curriculum's own monetary contract at the document-intake boundary.
findings.repair: Normalize monetary strings directly into Decimal from string (or integer cents), quantize explicitly and reconcile using the same type.

findings.evidence: Prose says EN-thousands '1,150.00' must be rejected/out-of-policy, but norm_total treats any comma+dot as PE and returns 1.15.
findings.attack: Runtime confirms the exact prohibited format is silently transformed into the wrong amount; scientific notation '1e3' is also accepted despite not being documented.
findings.defense: The fixture examples are limited to PE notation.
findings.impact: A syntactically plausible but wrong monetary value can autoenter cross-field validation.
findings.repair: Validate an explicit regex/grammar before conversion; reject unsupported mixed separators/scientific notation instead of guessing.

findings.evidence: norm_ruc rejects only [A-Za-z] then removes every remaining non-digit with \D.
findings.attack: Runtime shows Ñ, emoji and unsupported separators can be silently deleted, producing a plausible 11-digit RUC despite the prose 'una letra -> None'.
findings.defense: Common ASCII OCR confusions are caught.
findings.impact: Unexpected OCR corruption can be converted into an invented identity-like identifier.
findings.repair: Allowlist only documented benign separators; any other Unicode letter/symbol/control character -> None/review. Preserve raw value alongside normalized.

findings.evidence: SCHEMA is {'ruc':'str11','total':'float','fecha':'date'} but is never used to drive validation and does not encode requiredness despite prose saying schema defines required fields.
findings.attack: schema_version is manually printed while behavior is hardcoded elsewhere.
findings.defense: Pure normalization functions make concepts easy to learn.
findings.impact: Changing the schema does not change the validator; the advertised versioned contract is decorative.
findings.repair: Represent required/type/normalizer/rules in one schema object and have extraction/validation consume that exact version.

findings.evidence: validate accesses doc['total']; a missing total raises KeyError.
findings.attack: Theory says missing/low-quality docs accumulate reasons and one bad doc must not stop the batch.
findings.defense: The happy-path fixture always includes total.
findings.impact: A common OCR omission can crash processing instead of entering human review.
findings.repair: Validate presence/types before arithmetic; missing total -> total_missing reason and needs_review; never perform subtraction on absent/invalid values.

findings.evidence: T2 identifies RUC and total as critical, but validate checks only conf_ruc and ignores total/fecha confidence and fecha validity.
findings.attack: A low-confidence total can auto-pass if the arithmetic happens to match the same OCR-derived lines.
findings.defense: RUC is used as the focused didactic example.
findings.impact: The field-by-field abstention policy is not actually field-by-field.
findings.repair: Drive confidence/required checks from schema for every critical field and distinguish missing confidence from low confidence.

findings.evidence: validate returns ('needs_review', reasons) but no queue item contains source, page, bbox, raw/normalized values or review state.
findings.attack: Roadmap T3 and job relevance explicitly promise a human review queue as the product.
findings.defense: A status tuple can illustrate routing logic.
findings.impact: The reviewer cannot perform the evidence check the narrative describes.
findings.repair: Create a persisted/synthetic queue record with run/doc/page/field/raw/value/conf/bbox/reasons/status and reviewer decision fields.

findings.evidence: Theory says one needs_review document should not stop the nightly batch, but no theory code iterates documents or isolates per-document failures.
findings.attack: The code even has KeyError paths that could terminate a batch.
findings.defense: Batch orchestration may be deferred to S26.
findings.impact: Learner sees a throughput guarantee not demonstrated at this layer.
findings.repair: Add a tiny three-document fixture: ok/review/parser-error; prove all records yield terminal intake states without losing later documents.

findings.evidence: field_acc uses raw equality pred==true and divides by len(rows).
findings.attack: None==None is counted correct; an empty golden raises ZeroDivisionError. Missing ground truth/prediction need explicit scoring policy.
findings.defense: Current fixture contains complete labels.
findings.impact: Accuracy can be inflated by jointly missing fields and the evaluation crashes on an empty slice.
findings.repair: Define eligible labeled denominator, extraction/missing rates and conditional exact-match separately; return NA/not_evaluable for n=0.

findings.evidence: coverage_auto = auto/(auto+review), while T4-B introduces reject and OCR-failure/fallback outcomes.
findings.attack: Rejects/ocr_fail disappear from the denominator, making end-to-end automation coverage look better than intake reality.
findings.defense: The formula may mean coverage among admitted/extracted documents only.
findings.impact: Dashboard can report 0.7 when end-to-end intake auto coverage is 0.35 for the same 7 auto,3 review,5 reject,5 fail population.
findings.repair: Name denominators explicitly: admitted_selective_coverage and end_to_end_auto_rate; report reject/fail/rescan separately.

findings.evidence: field accuracy is computed on a 2-doc golden while coverage_auto uses unrelated hardcoded 7/3 counts.
findings.attack: You cannot judge whether a confidence threshold improves safe automation when accuracy and coverage are not computed from the same predictions/threshold.
findings.defense: The paragraph says they are different metrics and the tiny numbers are pedagogical.
findings.impact: The central abstention trade-off is described but not measured.
findings.repair: On one golden set, apply threshold t, compute coverage(t), error/accuracy on autoaccepted critical fields, review rate and threshold curves/slices.

findings.evidence: A 2-document golden is discussed next to per-field SLOs without uncertainty/sample counts beyond n implicit in code.
findings.attack: Two examples cannot support a reliability commitment.
findings.defense: It is explicitly a tiny synthetic teaching set, not a production benchmark.
findings.impact: A novice may confuse formula demonstration with evidence sufficient to set an SLO.
findings.repair: Separate 'toy calculation' from 'gate dataset'; always report n and uncertainty/error slices before promoting an SLO claim.

findings.evidence: Heading says hostile files, but implemented gate is only caller-provided MIME + compressed byte size; prose acknowledges this as layer 1.
findings.attack: Small malicious PDFs/images or spoofed MIME can still reach vulnerable parsers; file size alone does not bound page/content-stream/decompression work.
findings.defense: The section explicitly says signatures/isolated parsing/sandbox are production layer 2, so it does not fully claim security.
findings.impact: The heading/outcome can still be read as stronger protection than the executable code provides.
findings.repair: Call it 'layer-1 admission screen'; add at least a magic-signature negative fixture and resource/page/time budget concept, with deeper parsing explicitly deferred.

findings.evidence: gate_file directly indexes meta['mime'] and meta['n_bytes'].
findings.attack: Missing/malformed metadata raises KeyError rather than a controlled reject/review reason.
findings.defense: Fixtures always provide both fields.
findings.impact: Malformed intake metadata can stop the worker before the advertised fallback/review routing.
findings.repair: Validate metadata schema first; absent/invalid fields -> reject/review with explicit reason and continue batch.

findings.evidence: Learning outcome and T4-B prose promise ocr_fail -> human_rescan, but hostile_gate.py has no OCR failure path or rescan record.
findings.attack: The fallback is a major T4 ownership item, not a footnote.
findings.defense: gate_file runs before OCR, so failure may occur later.
findings.impact: The learner never demonstrates the terminal state that is supposed to prevent retry loops on corrupt documents.
findings.repair: Add an OCR result/error router with bounded retry for transient engine faults and human_rescan for deterministic/corrupt input, preserving reason/evidence.

findings.evidence: T4-B paragraph says bbox needs a controlled revisable rendition; callout says 'Borra imágenes crudas cuando el expediente solo necesita campos + bbox'.
findings.attack: If that raw/processed image is the only review rendition, deleting it makes bbox evidence unusable.
findings.defense: The paragraph itself asks for a controlled review copy and expiry.
findings.impact: A privacy instruction can destroy the evidence required for HITL/audit.
findings.repair: Define retention classes explicitly: keep the exact review rendition under access control until decision/retention expiry; delete redundant raw copies only after evidence lineage remains usable.

findings.evidence: Extracted OCR text is normalized as data but never marked untrusted before the next S25 LLM/prompting section.
findings.attack: Hostile documents can contain instructions/markup that should remain data, not control text for downstream models.
findings.defense: Prompt injection is explicitly owned by S25.
findings.impact: The S24->S25 handoff lacks a simple trust-boundary label.
findings.repair: Mark source/OCR text as untrusted_document_content and require downstream prompt/template separation; leave detailed prompt-injection defenses to S25.

findings.evidence: Dense terms include intake, bbox, confidence, schema, cross-field, golden, coverage_auto, HITL, fallback, deskew, crop, layout, adapter and runbook.
findings.attack: Many are introduced in English before a stable Spanish mental model, despite ZERO_TECH entry assumptions.
findings.defense: Literal API/data-contract names must remain recognizable to practitioners.
findings.impact: Language switching adds extraneous cognitive load to an already high-load document pipeline.
findings.repair: Introduce Spanish first plus literal term once: admisión (intake), caja delimitadora (bbox), confianza, esquema, validación entre campos, conjunto de referencia (golden), cobertura automática, revisión humana, alternativa/fallback.

rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.hypothesis: Any use of FakeOcrAdapter makes the section invalid.
rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.reason: Deterministic fake OCR is appropriate for parsing/abstention unit tests when clearly labeled; the defect is relying on it alone for the document-extraction gate.

rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.hypothesis: Any page below 300 dpi must be rejected.
rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.reason: 300 dpi is a useful Tesseract quality recommendation, not a universal hard boundary; the defect is the unexplained 300-vs-200 policy and fake metadata promotion.

rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.hypothesis: An 11-digit RUC must be validated against SUNAT or a checksum in S24.
rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.reason: The section explicitly limits itself to syntactic normalization and avoids claiming legal identity; no external legal-identity validation is required here.

rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.hypothesis: A fixed 0.85 confidence threshold is inherently wrong.
rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.reason: It is clearly labeled didactic; the required fixes are confidence-scale normalization and later empirical threshold evaluation on the same golden set.

rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.hypothesis: MIME+size must constitute a complete hostile-file security boundary in this lab.
rejected_or_bounded_hypotheses.reason: The prose explicitly calls it layer 1 and names stronger production layers; findings target the residual overstatement, missing metadata handling and unimplemented fallback rather than demanding a full malware sandbox in S24.

usable: abstention is a valid quality outcome
confidence does not prove business/legal correctness
orientation/preprocessing should occur before OCR when needed
matching or accounting mismatch is not a fraud label
golden evaluation should be field-specific rather than one aggregate score
misconception_risk: changing dpi metadata improves captured detail
raw Tesseract confidence is on a 0-1 scale
global y/x sorting is a general reading-order algorithm
key-value parsing can discard bbox/confidence safely
float is the canonical type for PEN
unsupported separators can be guessed safely
None==None should count as OCR field accuracy
auto/(auto+review) is always end-to-end automation coverage
bbox alone remains meaningful after geometric transforms or source-image deletion
carry_forward_to_S25: S25 must consume OCR fields only from a source_doc/page lineage with full hashes and evidence refs; S24 source_doc_id alone is not creditable.
Treat OCR/source text as untrusted_document_content; never concatenate it into instruction/system control text.
Do not treat S24 confidence 0.85 or status=auto as proof of correctness; preserve field confidence, review state and threshold version.
Preserve raw value plus normalized value; do not let an LLM repair RUC/money/date silently.
PEN values must use Decimal/integer cents rather than S24 float outputs.
If bbox evidence is required for review, retain the exact controlled rendition/coordinate mapping until review/retention expiry.
Rejected/ocr_fail/human_rescan records belong in S25 denominator/provenance; do not train/evaluate only on successful auto extracts.
